speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance, and are the lesions on the trunk and extremities arranged in a lacy or reticular pattern? I would also like to examine the rash closely to confirm these features. REQUEST IMAGES

text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a "slapped cheek" facial rash followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. To confirm this diagnosis, I will check for evidence of Parvovirus B19 infection. REQUEST TEST: Parvovirus_B19_IgM_antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Parvovirus B19 IgM test is negative, we must consider other causes for this rash pattern. Has the patient started any new medications in the past two weeks, and does the rash blanch when you press on it?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative Parvovirus B19 test, this presentation is highly suggestive of a viral exanthem or an alternative diagnosis like Roseola, though the age and rash timing are atypical. Have you noticed any joint pain or swelling, and has the rash spread to the palms or soles?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any respiratory distress, joint pains, or changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic "slapped cheek" facial rash and lacy body rash, the clinical diagnosis remains Erythema Infectiosum despite the negative IgM, which can occur if testing was done too early or late. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
